clue.text: Notorious guy was a novelist

definitions.meaning: Guy ..., the British diplomat who spied for the Soviet Union and defected in 1951
Anthony ..., author of A Clockwork Orange

explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' is lower-case in the surface but points to a man named Guy: the spy Guy Burgess, one of the Cambridge Five.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname is shared by a notorious Cold War spy and a celebrated English writer of fiction.

clue.text: Nasty daughter forsakes Uncle Dan

indicators.note: to forsake is to abandon, so the daughter leaves the words beside her

explanation.surface: A girl turns her back on a horrible relative called Dan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forsakes' takes the D out of UNCLE DAN, leaving the rest joined up as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unclean is dirty or foul, which is a sense of nasty.

clue.text: Raw colour

definitions.meaning: raw in the sense of inexperienced or unripe
the hue of grass and leaves

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both inexperienced (a raw recruit) and the colour of grass.

clue.text: The one who does French, say, at school

definitions.meaning: in grammar, the part of a sentence that performs the verb's action
French is an example of an area of study in the timetable

explanation.definitionFit: The grammatical doer of a verb and a school discipline such as French share this name.

clue.text: Our army collapsed when it closed?

definitions.text: Our army collapsed when it closed?

indicators.note: a collapsed structure falls into a jumble, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier wonders whether the forces fell apart because the weapons store was shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsed' rearranges OUR ARMY; the whole clue then suggests a military that crumbles once its weapons store is shut.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoury is the store of weapons an army depends on, so its closure would leave the troops helpless.

clue.text: Teacher has little time for talk

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher has only a moment for conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to 'rabbit' (on) is to talk at length about trivia.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal usage: to rabbit is to chatter on and on.

clue.text: Practitioner gets back work

parts.note: read as a medical practitioner whose job is manipulating patients' backs, rather than someone handed their work again

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone being returned their homework; the cryptic sense is a therapist whose work is on backs and joints.
explanation.definitionFit: This therapist treats the spine and musculoskeletal system, so backs are the daily work.

clue.text: Waves to the birds!

definitions.meaning: long heavy waves that roll in to shore
a family of brightly coloured birds named for their tumbling display flights

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both big rolling sea waves and a group of colourful birds famed for aerial tumbling.

clue.text: One can't catch a fat, old safe-breaker on the box

parts.note: Fingers was the nickname of a safe-cracking character in old British TV comedy; the box is television

explanation.surface: Someone describes a plump retired burglar seen on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the box' is British slang for television. The crook's nickname reflects light-fingered thieving.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone this is the standard jibe at a person who keeps dropping things or fluffs a catch.

clue.text: Care about piece of land

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tends a small plot with devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, used loosely for a plot of ground.

clue.text: Fly down with courage

parts.note: to feel down is to feel blue, unhappy
bottle is British slang for nerve or courage

explanation.surface: Someone takes a dive bravely, or descends in flight with nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like a verb but is the insect; 'bottle' as courage is British slang ('lose your bottle').
explanation.definitionFit: A bluebottle is a large blowfly with a metallic blue body.

clue.text: A scene made for session with the media

indicators.note: made in the sense of made into something else, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: Someone throws a tantrum during a press conference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the media' looks like the press, but here it is the plural of medium: spiritualists.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance is a meeting where mediums try to contact the dead.

clue.text: Well-made jockeys ride a lot

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre or shift about, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Well-turned-out riders spend a great deal of time in the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jockeys' reads as the riders who ride a lot, but it is a verb telling us to shuffle RIDE A LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailored clothing is cut to fit, hence neatly or well made.

clue.text: Stores can provide the roots of trees

indicators.note: the letters are made to provide a new word, a loose signal to rearrange them

explanation.surface: Shops are able to supply tree roots for gardeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trees' are family trees, not plants, so the roots are forebears.
explanation.definitionFit: Forebears are the origins from which a family tree grows.

clue.text: Dine out at length and see the city

annotationWithheld.why: Dine out at length and see the city (9): ana(DINE) gives EDIN, but no reading accounts for BURGH; the blog and commenters found no convincing parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Dine out at length and see the city

clue.text: The reason for some bird noises

annotationWithheld.why: The reason for some bird noises (5): CAUSE sounds like CAWS, but 'noises' is both the homophone signal and part of 'bird noises', one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: The reason for some bird noises

clue.text: Daughter associated with greedy king

explanation.surface: A girl is linked with a gluttonous monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: David was the biblical king of Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: David is a king of Israel in the Bible, and two Scottish kings bore the name.

clue.text: This fruit could be almost tropical

indicators.note: suggests the letters could be rearranged into another word
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A fruit that might well come from the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' removes the L from TROPICAL, and 'could be' rearranges TROPICA.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Applying polish — that's what Lancing does!

definitions.meaning: giving a final smooth surface or coat
the word Lancing ends in the letters I, N, G, so it finishes in that suffix; Lancing is also an English public school, hinting at a school for young ladies

explanation.walkthrough: Lancing is a boarding school in Sussex, which suggests a school that gives a final polish; the real trick is that the word itself ends with ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting the final coat or polish on work is giving it its final treatment.

clue.text: There's no way ahead: I'm finished

parts.note: I'm gives IM, the apostrophe dropped
passé means out of date, finished

explanation.surface: Someone at a dead end declares themselves done for.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock or dead end, a situation with no progress possible.

clue.text: A certain success is not affected …

definitions.meaning: a person bound to succeed, born with the gift for something

explanation.walkthrough: 'is' links the two senses, and the ellipsis runs on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a gifted person sure to succeed and someone free of airs.

clue.text: … but this kitchen appliance could be!

definitions.meaning: carrying 'affected' from the previous clue: someone who walks with dainty affected steps could be described by this word

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries 'affected' over from 21 Down: one who minces walks affectedly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a meat grinder and someone who minces, walking with exaggerated affectation.

clue.text: Boys kept in during awful beating

indicators.note: the boys are kept inside the other letters
awful suggests something mangled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: BB is the abbreviation for the Boys' Brigade

explanation.surface: Lads detained during a dreadful thrashing at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' looks like it describes the beating but rearranges the fodder to DRUING; 'kept in' signals the container. The Boys' Brigade is a Christian youth organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A drubbing is a heavy defeat or a thorough beating.

clue.text: Quick change of poster

indicators.note: a change of the word means its letters are altered in order

explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' is the musical tempo marking, Italian for fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is a musical direction meaning very fast.

clue.text: Standard design on some church lecterns

definitions.meaning: the Roman legion's banner, topped by a bird figure
many lecterns are carved as a bird with outspread wings supporting the Bible

explanation.definitionFit: The Roman military standard bore this bird, and many church lecterns are shaped like it.

clue.text: They supply data from the Telegraph

definitions.text: They supply data from the Telegraph

parts.words: They supply data from the Telegraph
parts.note: read as the cricket ground's telegraph, the board showing the score, rather than the newspaper

explanation.walkthrough: The Telegraph looks like the British newspaper, but at a cricket ground the 'telegraph' is the scoreboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Cards recording runs and wickets give the same figures shown on the cricket telegraph board.

clue.text: Clothing to boast about

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone shows off about their outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a word for clothing or dress, often distinctive.

clue.text: Craftsmen from Chester

indicators.note: the new word is made from these letters, a loose signal to rearrange

explanation.surface: Artisans hailing from the English city of Chester.
explanation.walkthrough: Chester is a city in north-west England; 'from' reads as origin but signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Etchers are artists who engrave designs on metal plates with acid.

clue.text: In the doorway they show leavers out

indicators.note: out suggests letters thrown out of order

explanation.surface: School leavers appear in the doorway as they go out.
explanation.walkthrough: A reveal is the side surface of a door or window opening; 'show' links, or offers the verb sense as a second hint.
explanation.definitionFit: In building, the reveals are the inner side faces of the opening framing a door.
